title: Some Moon Craters Are Colder Than Pluto's Surface

scenes.text: Some craters on the Moon are colder than Pluto.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter measured temperatures below minus three hundred ninety degrees Fahrenheit inside them.
Those craters sit near the poles, and they never see sunlight.
Meanwhile, at the Moon's equator at noon, the ground heats to about 250 degrees.
Same Moon, and a swing of more than six hundred degrees from place to place.
So yes: parts of the Moon are colder than Pluto.

description:
Some permanently shadowed craters on the Moon are colder than the surface of Pluto.
NASA's Diviner instrument measured temperatures as low as about minus 414 degrees Fahrenheit, while noon at the equator reaches over 250.
Which extreme surprised you more?
first_comment: If you could visit one place on the Moon, a hot noon or a frozen crater? Neither is survivable!
